issues.legal_issue: A special land-acquisition scheme for a welfare purpose is not rendered unreasonable under the equality guarantee merely because its procedures differ from those of the general acquisition law, where affected owners can object and compensation is determined by reference to market value after an inquiry with an appeal available.
material_facts: The scheme required the acquiring authority to notify owners and other interested persons and consider their objections before deciding to acquire land.
Compensation was based on the land’s market value on the date of the acquisition notice, determined after an inquiry in which interested persons could present their claims and evidence.
A court appeal was available against the compensation determination, and a further appeal was available in specified cases.
The scheme differed from the general acquisition law in its procedure and review mechanisms, but its market-value date was more favorable to owners.
issues.conclusion: The scheme’s acquisition and compensation provisions were not unreasonable or arbitrary under Article 14 on these grounds; differences from another acquisition law did not by themselves make it unconstitutional.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not permit one State’s law to be struck down merely by comparing it with another law on a similar subject; The State of Madhya Pradesh v. G.C. Mandawar and Sant Lal Bharti v. State of Punjab. A statute must be so arbitrary or unreasonable that it must be struck down. The specification of market value as the compensation basis is a sufficient guiding principle; State of Gujarat v. Shantilal Mangaldas. A landowner’s opportunity to establish market value before the prescribed authority, with an appeal from the resulting award, can provide an adequate means of challenging compensation; Raja Harish Chandra Raj Singh v. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer and Periyar and Pareekanni Rubbers Ltd. v. State of Kerala.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_a_special_we: A party challenges the constitutionality of a special land-acquisition scheme enacted for a welfare purpose.
predicates.owners_can_object_before_the_acquisition: The acquiring authority gives owners or interested persons an opportunity to object before deciding to acquire the land.
predicates.compensation_is_market_value_determined_: The authority determines compensation by assessing market value after an inquiry in which interested persons can present their claims and evidence.
predicates.compensation_determination_can_be_appeal: An affected person can appeal the compensation determination to a court.

issues.definition: When a special welfare acquisition scheme is challenged and owners can object, compensation is assessed by inquiry at market value, and that assessment can be appealed, the scheme is not unconstitutional on those procedural and compensation grounds.

issues.legal_issue: Requiring compensation for acquired land to be paid in instalments rather than promptly in a lump sum is unreasonable under the equality guarantee.
material_facts: The scheme required compensation above a specified threshold to be paid in equal annual instalments instead of in a lump sum.
The owner or another interested person could need the compensation promptly to obtain a new residence, agricultural land, or another means of re-establishing themselves.
issues.conclusion: The requirement to pay compensation in instalments was unconstitutional; the compensation had to be payable in a lump sum.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 invalidates a provision that is unreasonable in its effect on landowners. A person whose land is taken may need compensation forthwith to re-establish themselves, making compulsory deferred payment by instalments unreasonable.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_compulsory_l: A party challenges a rule governing payment for land taken through compulsory acquisition.
predicates.compensation_is_paid_in_instalments: The acquisition regime requires the compensation to be paid in separate instalments rather than in a lump sum.
predicates.landowner_needs_compensation_to_reestabl: The landowner may need the compensation promptly to obtain a new residence, land, or another means of re-establishing themselves.

issues.definition: If compulsory-acquisition compensation is paid in instalments and the landowner needs it to re-establish themselves, the installment requirement is unconstitutional.

issues.legal_issue: A special acquisition regime may apply to earlier proceedings commenced under the general acquisition law for the specified welfare purpose if no award had been made before the special regime took effect, but it does not undo an award already made.
material_facts: Proceedings had been started under the general acquisition law to acquire land for the welfare scheme before the special acquisition law commenced.
The special law provided for its application to such pending proceedings, subject to publication of a notice that the land was required for the specified purpose.
The Court noted that some earlier proceedings might have been completed and awards made before its decision, and clarified that the special law would have no effect in those cases.
issues.conclusion: Applying the special law to pending proceedings in which no award had been made was not unreasonable, but the law did not affect cases in which an award had already been made.
issues.legal_principle: The application of a new acquisition regime to pending proceedings is not unreasonable where the former regime ceases to govern acquisitions for the specified purpose and the new regime requires its own notice. The special law’s pending-case provision does not affect cases in which an award has already been made.

predicates.pending_acquisition_proceeding_for_a_spe: An acquisition proceeding for a specified welfare purpose remains pending when a new acquisition regime takes effect.
predicates.proceeding_started_under_an_earlier_acqu: The pending proceeding began under an acquisition regime that preceded the new one.
predicates.no_award_was_made_before_the_new_regime_: No award had been made in the proceeding before the new regime was applied.
predicates.required_new_notice_is_published: The acquiring authority publishes the notice required to bring the land within the new regime.

issues.definition: For a pending welfare-purpose acquisition begun under an earlier regime, the new regime may apply if no award had yet been made and the required notice is published, but it does not affect a case with an existing award.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of solatium does not by itself make an otherwise comparable land-acquisition regime unreasonable under the equality guarantee.
material_facts: The challenged slum-clearance provisions were substantially similar to the welfare acquisition provisions considered by the Court.
The slum-clearance provisions did not provide for payment of compensation in instalments.
They also did not provide for solatium in addition to compensation.
issues.conclusion: The slum-clearance acquisition provisions were constitutional; the absence of solatium did not make them unreasonable.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not require the State invariably to pay solatium in addition to reasonable compensation. The public interest in providing and maintaining public services is also relevant; Prakash Amichand Shah v. State of Gujarat.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_a_special_sl: A party challenges the constitutionality of a special regime for acquiring land for slum-related purposes.
predicates.compensation_is_not_deferred_in_instalme: The regime does not require compensation to be deferred through installment payments.
predicates.the_only_relevant_difference_is_no_solat: The regime is otherwise comparable to an acquisition regime upheld by the Court, and the relevant difference is that it provides no solatium.

issues.definition: When a special slum-acquisition regime is challenged, compensation is not deferred in instalments, and the only relevant difference is the absence of solatium, that absence alone does not make the regime unconstitutional.

issues.legal_issue: Once a special acquisition law governs land required for its specified welfare purpose, the land cannot instead be acquired for that purpose under the general acquisition law.
material_facts: After the special acquisition law had commenced, the State sought to acquire land under the general acquisition law for the welfare scheme.
The special law provided that land required for that purpose could be acquired only in accordance with its provisions.
The landowner sought to stop the proceedings under the general acquisition law.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings under the general acquisition law were quashed because the special law governed acquisition for that purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The special law made its acquisition process exclusive for land required for the specified welfare purpose, displacing the general acquisition law for that purpose.

predicates.challenge_to_an_acquisition_proceeding_u: A landowner challenges an acquisition proceeding brought under a general acquisition regime.
predicates.land_is_sought_for_a_purpose_governed_by: The land is being acquired for a purpose covered by a special acquisition regime that is in force.
predicates.special_regime_requires_exclusive_use_of: The special regime requires land acquired for that purpose to be acquired only through its own procedure.

issues.definition: When a landowner challenges a general-regime acquisition for a purpose governed by an exclusive special regime, the general-regime proceeding must be quashed.
